paragraph: Angola's [Law 22/11 of 17 June 2011](<https://lex.ao/docs/assembleia-nacional/2011/lei-n-o-22-11-de-17-de-junho/>) requires notice to the data protection agency, the APD, for a transfer to a country with adequate protection. A transfer to any other country needs the APD's authorisation. In the last twelve months, [Valor Económico reported on 26 June 2026](<https://valoreconomico.co.ao/artigo/apd-aplica-multas-milionarias-a-empresas-por-armazenarem-informacoes-pessoais-sem-autorizacao>) that the APD fined Crescer Tech about US$505,000 for a transfer to a cloud abroad without notice or authorisation. No source found says the APD has published a list of adequate countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the APD to publish one of them.

[Burundi Times reported in November 2026](<https://www.burunditimes.com/burundi-faces-data-protection-test-as-eac-advances-regional-rules/>) that Burundi promulgated Law No. 1/03 on the protection of personal data on 10 March 2026. Its Article 15 requires a country receiving personal data from Burundi to give an adequate level of protection, and the law allows other transfers where appropriate safeguards are in place. This law is the change found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the date it takes effect, and the agency it creates was still being set up. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

No stage is set. In the last twelve months, [the data protection authority's president said on 21 October 2026](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/2210-142651-adex-2026-mtn-benin-plaide-pour-une-cyber-resilience-proactive-a-lere-de-la-5g>) that the Code numérique requires critical servers to be sited on national territory. [Levellers says](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-benin>) Benin ratified the Malabo Convention by Decree 2024-772 of 1 February 2024 and deposited its instrument on 26 November 2024. No source found says what Benin's law rules on sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

Burkina Faso's data protection authority, the CIL, published an [application form in September 2026](<https://cil.bf/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/FORMULAIRE_ANNEXE-TRANSFERT-DE-DONNEES-A-LETRANGER-1.pdf>) for authorisation to transfer personal data to a foreign country. A transfer abroad needs the CIL's authorisation. In the last twelve months, the [Prime Minister's instruction of 23 January 2026](<https://digitalmagazine.bf/2026/02/20/burkina-faso-zoom-sur-les-12-chantiers-strategiques-du-ministere-de-la-transition-digitale-focus-sur-le-chantier-zero-donnee-a-lexterieur-souverainete-des-donnees-via-des-datacenters-locaux/>) called for public administration data hosted abroad to return to national datacentres. No source found says whether any transfer goes without the CIL's permission. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

[Mmegi reported on 25 November 2025](<https://www.mmegi.bw/business/govt-moves-to-in-house-local-data/news>) that Botswana's Data Protection Act, in effect since January 2025, allows transfers abroad only to approved countries. It also requires a copy of the data to remain in Botswana. [A DIAL expert comment of 15 June 2026](<https://dial.global/africas-digital-future-seamless-data-flows/>) says Botswana has an adequacy list on which only two African countries appear. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says how the copy requirement works beside transfers to approved countries. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time, with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

[Jurist Laurent-Fabrice Zengue wrote on 16 September 2025](<https://www.village-justice.com/articles/%EF%81%9Bcentrafrique%EF%81%9D-les-huit-forces-loi-relative-protection-des-donnees,54519.html>) that the Central African Republic's data protection law conditions transfers to a state outside CEMAC or ECCAS on sufficient protection in the recipient state. He added that other transfers face further requirements. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether any transfer goes without the authority's permission. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

[Decree 2015-79 of 4 February 2015](<https://www.artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/decret_2015_79.pdf>), issued under law 2013-450, requires prior authorisation from the telecoms regulator, ARTCI, to transfer personal data to a third country. The destination must give equal or higher protection. The decree names no route without authorisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Côte d'Ivoire's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 8 March 2023. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without ARTCI's permission each time.

[Authors at African Law & Business wrote on 23 December 2024](<https://www.africanlawbusiness.com/expert-views/key-features-of-cameroons-new-data-protection-law/>) that Cameroon's Act requires the data protection authority to authorise every cross-border transfer of personal data. In the last twelve months, [ACTPOL reported](<https://www.actpol.org/research/central-africa-laws-before-regulators-cameroon>) that the compliance period ended on 23 June 2026 and that the Authority has not been created. No route without authorisation is named. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Cameroon's signature of the Malabo Convention on 12 August 2021 and no deposit. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

[The Code du numérique, articles 262 to 270](<https://droitnumerique.cd/autorite-de-protection-des-donnees/>), creates a data protection authority. It authorises or refuses cross-border transfers of personal data to third states. Since 17 August 2024 a ministerial order has given those duties to the regulator ARPTIC. In the last twelve months, a [June 2026 legal summary](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-democratic-republic-of-congo>) said the Digital Code lets a transfer go where the destination gives equivalent protection. Otherwise the minister must authorise it. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking.

[Law no. 5-2025 of 29 March 2025](<https://www.sgg.cg/JO/2025/congo-jo-2025-15.pdf>) was published in the Journal officiel on 10 April 2025. It gives the data protection authority, the CNPD, the power to authorise cross-border transfers of personal data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says whether any transfer goes without the CNPD's permission. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Congo's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 24 September 2020. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

The Comoros Protection of Personal Data Law, enacted on 29 June 2021, [governs international transfers](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-the-comoros-data-protection-law>) on a risk-based model. The model rests on adequacy, appropriate safeguards and derogations. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Comoros's signature of the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2018 and no deposit. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

[Law 41/VIII/2013](<https://www.cnpd.cv/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Lei-n-41_VIII_2013-regime-juridico-geral-de-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais-das-pessoas-singulares.pdf>), published on 17 September 2013, allows transfer abroad only to a country with adequate protection. The authority, the CNPD, decides which states are adequate, and article 20 sets other grounds, such as consent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Cape Verde's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 13 November 2020. No source found says the CNPD has published its list of adequate countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the CNPD to publish one of them.

[The Code Numérique, published on 18 September 2025](<https://www.journalofficiel.dj/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/code-numerique.pdf>), bars a controller or processor from sending personal data to a third country unless the recipient ensures an equivalent and sufficient level of protection (article 99). Exceptions let data go on consent, contract, public interest, legal claims and vital interests. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Djibouti's signature of the Malabo Convention on 12 May 2023 and no ratification. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking.

[Digital Policy Alert says](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-algeria>) the 2023 personal data law allows transfers to states with adequate protection and with prior authorisation from the authority, the ANPDP. It also allows them on conditions such as explicit consent. [The US International Trade Administration's guide](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/algeria-digital-economy>) states that data localisation is mandatory under Law 18-07, in force since 10 August 2023. In the last twelve months, [the authority's Deliberation 04 of 15 July 2026](<https://anpdp.dz/ar/storage/2026/07/MOD-19-07-2026-v2.pdf>) treated publication on foreign-run platforms as a transfer abroad. No source found says the general localisation rule has been lifted. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

[Shura Law Firm states](<https://shuralawfirm.com/en/egypt-pdpl-compliance-checklist-what-to-do-before-the-october-31-2026-deadline/>) that transferring personal data outside Egypt requires a licence from the Personal Data Protection Centre and the person's consent. Full enforcement starts on 31 October 2026. In the last twelve months, [Legal 500 says](<https://www.legal500.com/guides/hot-topic/strategic-challenges-and-opportunities-in-cross-border-data-transfers-under-egypts-personal-data-protection-regime/?export-pdf=>), Executive Regulations were issued in November 2025 with a grace period to 1 November 2026. [ACTPOL said on 25 September 2026](<https://www.actpol.org/research/egypt-data-protection-deadline-north-africa>) that the regulations provide no standard contractual clauses. No source found says any transfer goes without the Centre's licence. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

[Levellers, in a page reviewed on 8 June 2026](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-eritrea>), states that Eritrea has no data protection legislation and no restriction on cross-border transfer of data in its law. The [UNECA digital trade profile](<https://dtri.uneca.org/v1/uploads/country-profile/eri-country-profile-en.pdf>) states that Eritrea does not require local data storage. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) shows no signature, ratification or deposit of the Malabo Convention. Preparing would need a transfer rule being written, or a rule in force that makes every transfer wait on the authority's permission.

[Techhive Advisory says](<https://www.techhiveadvisory.africa/insights/review-of-ethiopias-data-protection-act>) the Personal Data Protection Proclamation, published on 24 July 2024, makes transfers abroad depend on an adequacy decision by the Authority. Explicit consent, necessity or public registry purposes also serve. [Digital Policy Alert records](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/change/12100-data-localisation-requirements-in-personal-data-protection-proclamation-proclamation-no-13212024>) that the Proclamation also requires locally collected personal data to be stored on servers in Ethiopia. In the last twelve months, [Shega reported in November 2025](<https://shega.co/news/one-year-on-ethiopia-s-personal-data-protection-law-faces-a-slow-path-to-enforcement>) that the Authority had approved about 10 requests to transfer data abroad as a temporary measure. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

No stage is set. [Law 027/2023, article 27](<https://journal-officiel.ga/20087-027-2023-/>), promulgated on 11 July 2023, requires data judged confidential or sensitive to be hosted on national territory. The authority may grant a written derogation. In the last twelve months, [NotreAfrik states](<https://notreafrik.com/convention-de-malabo-ratifications/>) that Gabon ratified the Malabo Convention in 2026. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) shows no action. No source found says what Gabon's law rules on sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

[A 2025 roundup says](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/blog/data-protection-in-africa-roundup>) amendments to Ghana's Data Protection Act 2012 are in process and would add rules on international transfers. A draft Data Protection Act, 2025 has been published, and the roundup says it requires domestic storage of certain data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Ghana's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 13 May 2019. No source found says what the draft rules on sending personal data abroad. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

Guinea's [2016 law on cybersecurity and personal data protection](<https://assembleeguinee.org/loi-ndeg-l-2016-relative-la-cybersecurite-et-la-protection-des-donnees-caractere-personnel-en>) gives the data protection authority the power to approve transfers of personal data abroad. The text published in July 2016 names no constituted body and no appointed members. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says which transfers go without the authority's approval. No source found says the authority has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

A law-firm note of February 2026 describes Gambia's [Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act](<https://www.africanlawbusiness.com/expert-views/key-features-of-the-gambian-personal-data-protection-and-privacy-act/>), which provides a Commission that assesses cross-border transfers and may impose conditions on them. The note does not say the Commission is constituted or its members appointed. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says which transfers go without the Commission's permission. No source found says the Commission has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

No stage is set. [The African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that Guinea-Bissau signed the Malabo Convention on 31 January 2015. No ratification date is entered. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

No stage is set. In the last twelve months, on 25 March 2026 the [Chamber of Deputies approved ratification](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/la_camara_de_diputados_aprueba_la_ratificacion_de_dos_convenios_internacionales>) of the Malabo Convention. [The African Union says the foreign minister signed it](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/au-infrastructure-and-energy_equatorial-guinea-signs-the-malabo-convention-activity-7488275982521565184-ETtI>) on 28 July 2026. The [status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) shows no signature or deposit. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

Kenya's [Data Protection Act of 2019](<https://www.itweb.africa/article/kenya-tightens-cross-border-data-transfer-rules/WnpNgq21y6kMVrGd>) governs sending personal data abroad. In the last twelve months, a report of 9 September 2026 said the Data Commissioner's guidance sets the conditions for a lawful transfer, including the safeguards required and the mechanisms for adequate protection. No source found says which transfers go without the Commissioner's permission. No source found says a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation has been published. [Cabinet approved the Malabo Convention in 2025](<https://citizen.digital/article/stakeholders-urge-ratification-of-malabo-convention-for-effective-digital-governance-in-kenya-n389789>), and the National Assembly has yet to approve it. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

No stage is set. [The African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) shows no signature, ratification or deposit of the Malabo Convention by Liberia. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

No stage is set. [Central Bank Circular No. 18 of 1 June 2025](<https://informatics.ly/en/session/personal-data-protection-regulation-session/>) bars banks, fintechs and payment providers from storing personal data outside Libya from 1 July 2026. It covers those sectors only. [The African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) shows no signature or ratification of the Malabo Convention. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad in general. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, with no rule on sending it abroad.

Lesotho's [Data Protection Act of 2012](<https://zmayetlaw.co.ls/lesothos-outdated-data-protection-act-no-commissioner-no-teeth-what-should-change-next/>) is in force and has cross-border transfer rules modelled on the SADC rules. A law firm wrote in October 2025 that the Commission and Commissioner have not been appointed, so no authority exists to approve transfer mechanisms. It also wrote that standard contractual clauses and binding corporate rules are not yet in place. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Lesotho's signature of the Malabo Convention on 30 November 2023. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

The Council of Europe's committee described Morocco's [law 09-08](<https://rm.coe.int/16806fdcb3>) in October 2012. Articles 43 and 44 protect transfers of personal data to foreign countries, in particular where the country does not provide an adequate level of protection. [Morocco's 2015 adequacy list](<https://dial.global/africas-digital-future-seamless-data-flows/>) names the countries personal data may be sent to, and the DIAL research group records that it did not recognise a single African country. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) shows no signature or ratification of the Malabo Convention. Mature would need ratification of the Malabo Convention or the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol, or treating an African partner's protection as good enough in practice.

No stage is set. [The African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Madagascar's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 17 July 2025. The [Constitutional Court ruled on 10 July 2024](<https://www.hcc.gov.mg/?p=9255>) that the Convention and the authorising law conform to the Constitution. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

Mali's [law 2013-015 of 21 May 2013](<https://primature.ml/apdp-autorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>) lets a controller transfer personal data to a foreign state when the data protection authority finds the receiving state's protection sufficient. Where contract clauses or internal rules cover a transfer, the authority decides. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says a transfer may go without the authority's decision, or that it has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. [The African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) shows no signature, ratification or deposit by Mali. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

[INTIC reports](<https://intic.gov.mz/proposta-de-lei-de-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais-segue-para-debate-na-assembleia-da-republica/>) that Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved a Personal Data Protection Bill on 3 March 2026 for the Assembly of the Republic. It allows international transfers only where equivalent protection is assured. In the last twelve months this bill is the new step, and it is not in force, so no transfer condition binds controllers until the Assembly passes it. [A UNECA, GIZ and African Union inception report of 19 June 2025](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/sites/default/files/resources/documents/TICID/data-governance-framework-mozambique/en_project_inception_report_mozambique_data_governance_framework.pdf>) states that Mozambique ratified the Malabo Convention in 2019. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

Mauritania's [law 2017-020 of 22 July 2017](<https://natlex.ilo.org/dyn/natlex2/natlex2/files/download/112890/MRT-112890.pdf>) bars a controller from sending personal data to a third country unless it ensures a sufficient level of protection. [Deliberation 004/2025 of 14 July 2025](<https://www.apd.mr/%d8%a7%d9%84%d9%85%d8%af%d8%a7%d9%88%d9%84%d8%a9-%d8%b1%d9%82%d9%85-004-2025-%d8%aa%d8%ad%d8%af%d8%af-%d8%b4%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b7-%d9%88%d9%82%d9%88%d8%a7%d8%b9%d8%af-%d8%a5%d8%ac%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%a1%d8%a7/>) sets the conditions for transfers abroad, and the authority publishes and updates a list of countries it judges adequate. [NotreAfrik reports](<https://notreafrik.com/convention-de-malabo-ratifications/>) that Mauritania ratified the Malabo Convention by May 2023. In the last twelve months, the authority's [meeting of 29 April 2026](<https://www.apd.mr/fr/reunion-mensuelle-ordinaire-de-lautorite-de-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel-16/>) listed amendments to deliberations 004/2025 and 005/2025. No source found shows the outcome of the April 2026 amendments.

Mauritius's [Data Protection Act 2017](<https://dataprotection.govmu.org/AnnualReports/265-26-DPO%20AR%202024-SOFT%20COPY.pdf>) sets a rule on transfers in section 36. The Data Protection Office reports that in 2024 it authorised 112 cross-border transfers and rejected 12 under that section. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says which transfers go without authorisation. No source found says the Office has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. The [African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records ratification of the Malabo Convention on 6 March 2018. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

Malawi's [Data Protection Act](<https://itlawco.com/focus-areas/data-protection-and-privacy/malawis-data-protection-act-2024-an-overview/>) came into force on 3 June 2024. Sections 38 to 40 restrict transfers of personal data outside Malawi unless the receiving country has adequate protection or binding corporate rules are in place. The [Act of 2024](<https://www.mca.ac.mw/mca-siteup/uploads/Data%20Protection%20Act%202024.pdf>) also lets a transfer go on a contractual clause, a code of conduct, certification or consent. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the authority has published a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the authority to publish one of them.

On 4 August 2026 [opposition member Rodney Cloete told the Windhoek Observer](<https://observer24.com.na/mp-raises-concerns-about-data-control-of-smart-city-grant-from-china/>) that Namibia has no data protection statute, so no rules govern cross-border transfers of data. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found shows a law, regulation or draft that sets a condition for sending personal data abroad. The [African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Namibia's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 25 January 2019. Preparing would need a transfer rule being written, or a rule in force that makes every transfer wait on the authority's permission.

No stage is set. The [African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records Niger's ratification of the Malabo Convention on 22 February 2022. It also records deposit on 16 March 2022. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law, regulation or draft that governs sending personal data abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, or a source from the past three years saying nothing protects personal data sent abroad.

Nigeria's [Data Protection Act 2023](<https://cert.gov.ng/ngcert/resources/Nigeria_Data_Protection_Act_2023.pdf>) has a Part VIII on cross-border transfers, in sections 41 to 43. [The Commissioner says](<https://www.vanguardngr.com/2025/04/nigeria-joins-global-cross-border-privacy-forum/>) the Commission decides the adequacy of other countries' protection as a basis for transfer. The Commission also approves binding corporate rules, codes and certification mechanisms. In the last twelve months, a [central bank circular of 15 June 2026](<https://complyan.com/nigerias-cbn-data-localisation-directive-what-banks-and-fintechs-must-do-before-2027/>) kept payment data in Nigeria, for payment operators only. No source found says the Commission has published a list of adequate countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation. Operating would need the Commission to publish one of them.

Rwanda's [law 058/2021 of 13 October 2021](<https://dpo.gov.rw/fileadmin/DPO/ComplianceTools/-_Standard_Contractual_Clauses_for_Transfer_Personal_Data_Outside_Rwanda_.pdf>) sets the rule in article 49. [Digital Policy Alert says](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-rwanda>) it allows transfers abroad through the authority's authorisation, the person's consent or specific exceptions. It also says the law generally requires personal data to be stored in Rwanda unless the supervisory authority grants a certificate. A [market brief of July 2025](<https://cms.d4dhub.eu/assets/Initiatives/Data-Governance-in-Africa/Digital-Investment-Facility/2507_Country-Market-Briefs/Data-Center-Market-Brief-Rwanda.pdf>) says there is no blanket requirement. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

[The Sudanese Center for Policy Studies reported on 19 July 2026](<https://sudancps.com/en/2026/07/19/sudans-privacy-gap-balancing-digital-transformation-and-data-laws-intro/>) that no statute governs cross-border transfer of data in Sudan. [Global Voices wrote on 21 October 2023](<https://advox.globalvoices.org/2023/10/21/the-ongoing-conflicts-impact-on-ict-and-digital-transformation-efforts-in-sudan/>) that Sudan has no law imposing data localisation. [The African Union status list](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that Sudan signed the Malabo Convention on 15 March 2023. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No ratification is on record. Preparing would need a transfer rule being written, or a rule in force that makes every transfer wait on the authority's permission.

Article 9 of [Law 2008-12](<https://www.mondaq.com/data-protection/693598/data-security-and-cybercrime-in-senegal>) bars a data owner from sending data to a country that does not give sufficient protection. [A law-firm note of 11 May 2018](<https://www.mondaq.com/data-protection/693598/data-security-and-cybercrime-in-senegal>) says the data protection authority must be informed and its authorisation sought. It names no route that avoids authorisation. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [The African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that Senegal ratified the Malabo Convention on 3 August 2016. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

No stage is set. [Regulation 22(3) of the 2020 subscriber registration regulations](<https://www.parliament.gov.sl/uploads/statutory_instruments/S.%20I.%20Subscribers%20Identification%20and%20Registration%20Management%20Regulations,%202020.pdf>) bars sending subscribers' registration information outside Sierra Leone, unless the National Telecommunications Commission gives prior approval. [The African Union status list of 2 February 2026](<https://au.int/sites/default/files/treaties/29560-sl-AFRICAN_UNION_CONVENTION_ON_CYBER_SECURITY_AND_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_0.pdf>) records that Sierra Leone signed the Malabo Convention on 29 January 2016. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets a condition on sending personal data in general abroad. Absent would need a rule keeping personal data in general in the country, with no rule on sending it abroad.

Articles 30 and 31 of [Law No. 005 of 2023](<https://moct.gov.so/en/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Somalia-Data-Protection-Act-2.pdf>), signed on 22 March 2023, bar a controller from sending personal data abroad. Two cases are exempt: the recipient gives adequate protection, or a stated exception applies. The law lets data go where the recipient is bound by law, binding corporate rules or contract clauses, and on the person's consent. In the last twelve months, [civil society called on 20 July 2026](<https://sonsaplatform.org/somali-civil-society-issued-advocacy-position-on-the-ratification-of-the-malabo-convention>) for Somalia to sign and ratify the Malabo Convention. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking.

No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found sets out a law or regulation on sending personal data abroad, or a data localisation rule. Articles 19 and 20 of [Law No. 03/2016](<https://www.dataguidance.com/sites/default/files/STP%20-%20Lei%20n.%C2%BA%2003_2016%20-%20Lei%20de%20Garantia%20e%20Protec%C3%A7%C3%A3o%20dos%20Dados%20Pessoais%20d....pdf>), promulgated on 18 March 2016, allow personal data to leave the country only where the receiving legal system gives adequate protection. A [factsheet updated on 24 June 2022](<https://dataprotection.africa/sao-tome-and-principe/>) adds a route by notification with the person's unequivocal consent, and lists the authority as operational. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries or model contract terms has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish a way to send data without asking: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

[The Eswatini Data Protection Authority's 2024 application form](<https://edpa.org.sz/assets/documents/APPLICATION%20FORM_%20TRANSFER.pdf>) requires authorisation before personal data leaves the country. The applicant supplies the recipient country's law, contracts and an impact assessment. In the last twelve months, [the Ministry of ICT reported on 10 July 2026](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ministry-of-ict-eswatini_the-minister-of-information-communications-activity-7481421459043770369-IcuH>) a workshop with senators on ratifying the Malabo Convention. No source found says any transfer goes without authorisation. No list of countries or model contract terms has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

[DLA Piper reports](<https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=SC>) that Seychelles' Data Protection Act 2023 came into force on 22 December 2023. It permits transfers outside Seychelles only where the transfer ensures an adequate level of protection, and it allows transfers with appropriate safeguards or legal mechanisms. [The Information Commission's 2025 annual report](<https://www.infocom.sc/wp-content/uploads/Annual-Report-2025.pdf>) counts 6 data transfer cases handled as guidance and advice. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries, model contract terms or general authorisation has been found. Operating would need the authority to publish one of them.

It says transfers need notification or prior authorisation by the authority, ANSICE, without saying which need which. No change has been found in the last twelve months. [ACTPOL, citing the African Union list of 2 February 2026](<https://www.actpol.org/research/central-africa-laws-before-regulators-cameroon>), says Chad signed the Malabo Convention without ratifying it. No list of countries or model contract terms has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

Articles 50 to 52 of [Organic Law 2004-63 of 27 July 2004](<https://legislation-securite.tn/latest-laws/loi-organique-n-2004-63-du-27-juillet-2004-portant-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel/>) allow transfer of personal data abroad only to a country with an adequate level of protection. The law requires prior authorisation of the authority, INPDP, in every case. [DIAL wrote on 15 June 2026](<https://dial.global/africas-digital-future-seamless-data-flows/>) that Tunisia's 2018 adequacy list names only five African countries. In the last twelve months, [lawyer Zied El Air wrote in 2026](<https://www.elair-avocat.com/en/news/gdpr-tunisian-law-ai-obligations-2026/>) that organic bill 095/2025 contains a revised framework for international transfers. Part V of the [Personal Data Protection Act, published on 13 June 2023](<https://www.pdpc.go.tz/media/media/THE_PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_ACT.pdf>), sets rules for transfer to a state with adequate protection and to a state without it. [The Commission says](<https://pdpc.go.tz/>) it regulates transfers through a cross-border data transfer permit, and reports 121 permits offered by August 2026. No source found says a transfer to an adequate country goes without a permit. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No list of countries, model terms or general authorisation has been found. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.

[CIPESA says](<https://cipesa.org/2025/07/ugandan-regulator-finds-google-in-breach-of-countrys-data-protection-law-orders-local-registration/>) section 19 of Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act 2019 requires data sent abroad to go to a country with equivalent protection, with the person's consent. The regulator applied the rule against Google on 18 July 2025. In the last twelve months, [the decision of 20 February 2026 on WhatsApp](<https://adlegalug.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/PDPO-Decision-in-Ad-legal-International-Ltd-v-WhatsApp-LLC-Meta-Platforms-Inc.pdf>) ordered an adequacy assessment by the company. It names no list of countries or model terms. Operating would need the regulator to publish a way to send data without asking: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

[South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act](<https://infotrust.com/articles/south-africas-protection-of-personal-information-act-popia/>) bars sending personal information abroad unless the recipient is under adequate legal protection. Transfers may also go on the person's consent or where a contract requires it, with no authorisation step. [The same source, of January 2024](<https://infotrust.com/articles/south-africas-protection-of-personal-information-act-popia/>), says the Act names no countries with adequate protection and no way to recognise them. The sender judges adequacy itself. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a published route that needs no case-by-case judgment: a list of countries, model contract terms or a general authorisation.

[The Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021](<https://www.parliament.gov.zm/sites/default/files/documents/acts/Act%20No.%203%20The%20Data%20Protection%20Act%202021_0.pdf>), enacted on 24 March 2021, sets conditions in sections 70 and 71 for sending personal data out of Zambia. [In February 2024 the Commissioner said section 70(1) requires data to be processed and stored in Zambia, with exceptions the Minister sets](<https://zambia24.com/2024/02/23/data-protection-commission-to-initiate-inspections-and-enforcement/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found gives the exceptions the Minister has set. No approved contract terms or list of countries have been found. Establishing would need a rule in force with no rule keeping personal data in general at home.

[POTRAZ guideline CDPG 5 of 2024](<https://www.veritaszim.net/sites/veritas_d/files/05%20Guideline%20on%20cross%20border%20transfer.pdf>), issued on 13 November 2024, bars controllers from sending personal data abroad unless they notify the Authority. They must also run an impact assessment and show consent, adequate protection and a data-sharing agreement. In the last twelve months, [POTRAZ reported on 26 December 2025](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/cybersecurity/zimbabwe-to-guide-southern-africa-in-data-protection-capacity-building>) that 24 transfers have been authorised. No source found says which transfers go without prior authorisation. Establishing would need a rule in force that lets some transfers go without permission each time.
